gloss: pour out (a libation); cast (metal); drink offering; cast image; set, install
summary: נָסַךְ is to pour out, above all wine poured to God as a libation, and to pour molten metal, casting an image. נֶסֶךְ is the drink offering of wine that went with the burnt offering and grain offering every day and at every feast of Lev 23 (Exo 29:40; Lev 23:13; Num 15:5–10; 28:7), and also a cast image; מַסֵּכָה is a cast image, the calf of Horeb first (Exo 32:4). Scripture also uses the root of setting a king in place (“I have set my king on Zion”, Psa 2:6) and of princes (נָסִיךְ, Jos 13:21), and, with no clear tie to the rest, of a woven covering or web (Isa 25:7; Jdg 16:13). Ugaritic, Aramaic and Phoenician have the same verb “pour”, and Phoenician the same “cast metal” and “libation”.

words.summary: What is poured out: almost always the wine poured to Yahweh with the burnt offering and grain offering, set by the hin for each animal; poured to other gods by Judah in Jeremiah's day. Four times the cast metal image of an idol.

senses.definition: Wine (once “strong drink”) poured out to Yahweh in the holy place as a fixed part of the burnt offering: a fourth of a hin for a lamb, a third for a ram, a half for a bull, “a scent of pleasing to Yahweh”, offered with the daily offering, the sabbaths, new moons and every appointed feast.

evidence.note: “Wine for the נֶסֶךְ, a fourth of the hin, you shall make with the burnt offering or the sacrifice, for each lamb.”
A third of a hin of wine for a ram.
Half a hin of wine for the נֶסֶךְ with a bull: “a gift, a scent of pleasing to Yahweh”.
With the daily lamb: “in the holy place pour out a נֶסֶךְ of strong drink to Yahweh”; noun and verb together.
The daily lamb with flour, oil, and “a fourth of the hin of wine for a נֶסֶךְ”.
With the sheaf of the firstfruits: “its נֶסֶךְ, wine, a fourth of the hin”.
The offerings of the feast of Weeks “with their grain offering and their drink offerings”.
The appointed times of Yahweh: “burnt offering and grain offering, sacrifice and drink offerings, the thing of a day on its day”.
The first: Jacob pours a נֶסֶךְ on the pillar at Bethel, and oil on it.
The Nazirite's ram with its grain offering and its drink offering.
The new moons: the measures of wine per animal again.
The drink offerings of all the appointed times, besides vows and freewill offerings.
“The jars of the נֶסֶךְ” on the table of the presence.
“Grain offering and drink offering are cut off from the house of Yahweh”: the priests mourn.
Yahweh may leave a blessing behind him, a grain offering and a drink offering.
In the house Ezekiel is shown, the prince provides the drink offering at the feasts, new moons and sabbaths.
Sacrifices “with their drink offerings” when Solomon is made king.

senses.definition: Drink offerings poured to the queen of the heavens, to Baal and the host of the heavens, on the roofs of Jerusalem and on every high hill: the same act turned to idols.

evidence.note: “They pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke me.”
“To burn incense to the queen of the heavens and to pour out drink offerings to her.”
On every high hill and leafy tree “they poured out there their drink offerings”.
“To them you have poured out (שָׁפַךְ) a drink offering.”
“I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood”: the libations of those who hasten after another god.

senses.definition: An idol of molten metal, beside the carved image: what is poured into a mould.

evidence.note: “My carved image and my נֶסֶךְ commanded them”: set beside פֶּסֶל.
“Every refiner is put to shame by the carved image, for his נֶסֶךְ is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.”
The same words.
“Their cast images are wind and emptiness.”

evidence.locator: Gen.35.14, נֶסֶךְ → σπονδήν; Lev.23.13, Num.15.5, Num.28.7 the same; σπονδή renders נֶסֶךְ ×27 in the alignment. The New Testament does not use the noun, only its verb σπένδω.

parallels.note: The grain offering, the drink offering's constant companion: the two cut off together and given back together.
The carved image, beside the נֶסֶךְ as cast image.

phrases.gloss: a drink offering of strong drink
pour out drink offerings to other gods
the jars of the drink offering

words.gloss: cast image, molten idol; libation; covering, web
words.summary: Mostly an idol cast in metal: the calf of Horeb, the gods Israel was forbidden to make, Micah's image, the calves of Jeroboam. Once perhaps a libation poured to seal a pact (Isa 30:1). Twice a covering or something woven (Isa 25:7; 28:20); for that sense no tie to “pour” or “cast” has been found.

senses.definition: An image made by pouring molten metal, as Aaron made the calf from the people's gold; named beside the carved image as the two kinds of idol.

evidence.note: Aaron takes the gold, shapes it with a tool, and makes “a calf of מַסֵּכָה”: “These are your gods, Israel.”
“Gods of מַסֵּכָה you shall not make for yourself.”
“You had made yourselves a calf of מַסֵּכָה.”
“Cursed is the man who makes a carved image or a cast image, the work of the craftsman's hands.”
Two hundred pieces of silver given to a refiner, who makes of them a carved image and a cast image.
“Images of their cast metal” of the Canaanites, to be destroyed.
Israel “made for themselves a cast image, two calves”.
The gold covering of the cast images, thrown away as unclean.
Those who say to a cast image, “You are our gods”.
“They have made for themselves a cast image of their silver… all of it the work of craftsmen.”
“A cast image and a teacher of lies”: mute, with no breath in it (2:19).
Stephen expounds Exo 32:4: “they made a calf in those days and offered sacrifice to the idol”.

senses.definition: Once, with the verb נָסַךְ, a libation poured out, apparently in making the alliance with Egypt that Judah sought without Yahweh's counsel. Some read the phrase instead as “weave a web”, an alliance spun together; the parallel “take counsel” fits either.

evidence.note: “To take counsel, but not from me, and to pour a מַסֵּכָה, but not of my spirit”, going down to Egypt (30:2).

senses.definition: A spread covering: the web woven over all the nations that Yahweh will swallow up on his mountain, and a blanket too narrow to wrap oneself in. How it ties to “pour” or “cast” is not clear; the verb in Isa 25:7 is the passive “woven”, and Hebrew סָכַךְ, “cover, weave” (Psa 139:13), may lie behind it.

evidence.note: “The covering that covers all the peoples, and the מַסֵּכָה woven over all the nations”, parallel to לוֹט, covering.
“The bed is too short to stretch out on, and the מַסֵּכָה too narrow to wrap oneself in.”

evidence.locator: Exo.32.4, מַסֵּכָה → χωνευτόν (printed ξωνευτὸν in the alignment); χωνευτός and χώνευμα render מַסֵּכָה in most places. Not used in the New Testament.

parallels.note: The carved image: the two together are the whole of idolatry.
Covering, parallel to the woven מַסֵּכָה.

phrases.gloss: a carved image and a cast image

words.gloss: pour out (a libation); cast (metal); set, install; (passive) woven
words.summary: To pour out: wine or water to Yahweh, drink offerings to idols, a spirit of deep sleep, and molten metal to cast an image. Twice it is setting someone in place, a king on Zion and Wisdom before the earth; once, as a passive participle, “woven”, which no cognate yet ties to the rest.

stems.gloss: pour out; cast (an image); set, install; (passive participle) woven

senses.definition: Pour out wine as a drink offering; and once of Yahweh pouring a spirit of deep sleep over the prophets, as a liquid is poured over something.

evidence.note: “And a drink offering you shall not pour on it”: no libation on the altar of incense.
“They will not pour out wine to Yahweh.”
“Yahweh has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep, and has closed your eyes.”
“To pour a libation, but not of my spirit”; see מַסֵּכָה.

senses.definition: Pour molten metal into a mould: the craftsman's work in making an idol, before the smith overlays it with gold.

evidence.note: “The image! A craftsman casts it, and a smith overlays it with gold.”
“Who has formed a god, or cast an image, that profits nothing?”, parallel to יָצַר, form.

senses.definition: Set a king in his place and office. Whether the image is of pouring (the king is Yahweh's anointed, Psa 2:2) or of something cast and set firm, the verses do not say; the sense is plain from the context.

evidence.note: “But I, I have set my king on Zion, the mountain of my holiness”, against the kings of the earth set against Yahweh and his anointed (2:2).
The apostles read Psa 2 of “your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed”.

senses.definition: Once, of the web “woven” over all the nations. No cognate of נסך means weave, and how this sense ties to the root's “pour” is not known.

evidence.note: “The web woven (הַנְּסוּכָה) over all the nations.”

stems.gloss: be set up, or be formed

senses.gloss: be set up, or be formed
senses.definition: Wisdom's word for her own beginning: set up, or formed, from everlasting before the earth. Its parallels are “Yahweh possessed me” and “I was brought forth” in birth (חוֹלָלְתִּי), and Psa 139:13 has סָכַךְ for God forming a child in the womb, so “formed” is as likely as “set up”.

evidence.note: “From everlasting I was נִסַּכְתִּי, from the beginning, from the earliest times of the earth.”
“Yahweh possessed me at the beginning of his way.”
“When there were no depths I was brought forth.”
“You wove me (תְּסֻכֵּנִי) in my mother's womb”, of the near root סכך.

senses.definition: David pours out the water his three men brought from Bethlehem's well, the Chronicler's form of 2Sa 23:16.

evidence.note: “David would not drink it, and he poured it out to Yahweh.”

senses.definition: Make a libation: pour out wine, or water, to Yahweh at an altar or pillar, or to other gods; almost always with נֶסֶךְ as its object.

evidence.note: Jacob “poured a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it”.
“In the holy place pour out a drink offering of strong drink to Yahweh.”
David “poured it out to Yahweh”: “Is it not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?” (23:17).
Ahaz offers on his new altar and pours out his drink offering.
To other gods.
“I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood.”

senses.definition: Of the golden jars and bowls of the table of the presence, “with which it is poured out”: the vessels for the drink offering.

evidence.note: “Its jars and its bowls, with which it shall be poured out; of pure gold.”
The same jars are “the jars of the drink offering”.

greek.gloss: pour out a libation; (passive) be poured out as a drink offering

evidence.locator: Gen.35.14, וַיַּסֵּךְ → ἔσπεισεν; Num.28.7, הַסֵּךְ → σπείσεις; 2Sa.23.16, וַיַּסֵּךְ → ἔσπεισεν; Jer.44.17–19 the same verb

evidence.note: “If I am even poured out as a drink offering (σπένδομαι) on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice.”
“I am already being poured out as a drink offering (σπένδομαι), and the time of my departure has come.”

parallels.note: Form, fashion: casting an image beside forming a god.
Burn incense: the two acts of worship done together to the queen of the heavens.

words.summary: Four times a prince or chief among men, set beside shepherds and nobles; once a libation and once a cast image, as נֶסֶךְ is. Akkadian nasīku, a tribal chief, is the same word in the prince sense; whether the prince is “one installed” (Psa 2:6) or “one anointed”, the verses do not say.

senses.definition: A leader under or beside a king: the Midianite chiefs who were Sihon's princes, the princes of the north, and the leaders Israel will raise up against Assyria.

evidence.note: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, “the princes of Sihon”: chiefs of Midian under the Amorite king.
“Make their nobles (נְדִיבֵמוֹ) like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna.”
“Seven shepherds and eight princes of men” raised up against Assyria.
“The princes of the north, all of them”, gone down to the pit.

senses.definition: Wine poured out to the gods, as נֶסֶךְ.

evidence.note: The gods “who ate the fat of their sacrifices, drank the wine of their libations”.

senses.definition: A cast metal image carried off with the gods of a conquered land.

evidence.note: “Their gods with their cast images, with their precious vessels of silver and gold.”

parallels.note: Noble, in parallel with the princes.

words.summary: The web on the loom into which Delilah wove Samson's hair. With the woven מַסֵּכָה and the passive “woven”, it is one of the root's weaving words, whose tie to “pour” is not known; no cognate shares it.

senses.definition: The threads stretched on a loom, into which the weft is woven and which a peg holds fast.

evidence.note: “If you weave (תַּאַרְגִי) the seven locks of my head with the web.”
He pulls away “the peg of the loom and the web”.

words.summary: Scripture's one Aramaic use: Nebuchadnezzar orders an offering and incense to be offered to Daniel.

senses.definition: Present an offering to someone as to a god, the verb of pouring a libation used of offering in general.

evidence.note: The king falls on his face before Daniel and commands “to offer (לְנַסָּכָה) to him an offering and sweet savours”.

senses.definition: The drink offerings that go with the bulls, rams and lambs on the altar at Jerusalem, as in the law.

evidence.note: Artaxerxes' letter: buy “bulls, rams, lambs, with their grain offerings and their drink offerings” and offer them on the altar.

cognates.gloss: to pour; (G passive or N) be poured
cognates.note: Imperative sk (KTU 1.3 III 16) and ysk (KTU 1.17 VI 36): the same verb “pour” as Hebrew.

evidence.note: “sk imper. 1.3:III:16 … ysk Gp/N 1.17:VI:36 … ‘to pour’ (H. nāsak, yissōkū …)”

evidence.locator: SEM000276 nsk [pour] V, UGC003167 nsk [G/Gpass] V

cognates.note: The Targums' verb for Hebrew נָסַךְ: Targum Onkelos Exo 30:9, Targum Num 28:7.

evidence.note: “esp. to offer a libation. Targ. Cant. IV, 15”; Pa. “Targ. Ex. XXX, 9”; Hithpa. “Targ. Num. XXVIII, 7”.

evidence.locator: SEM000276 nsk [pour] V, ARM019726 NSK [pour] V

evidence.note: Targ. O. Exo 29:40; pl. נִסְכִּין, Targ. Jer 19:13.

cognates.gloss: cast metal; a bar of silver or gold
cognates.note: The same Aramaic word that means libation also means metal that has been cast, as Hebrew נֶסֶךְ is both.

evidence.note: “cast metal … Esp. a piece of silver or gold, bar, opp. to מטבע, coined metal” (B. Kam. 96b).

cognates.gloss: cast objects of metal; make an offering; (noun) caster of metal
cognates.note: Punic hnskm šbrzl “the casters of iron objects” (KAI 100.17); nsk ḥrṣ “casters of gold”.

evidence.locator: p. 329, N-S-K I and NSK II
evidence.note: “v. qal 1. CAST objects of metal … 2. MAKE AN OFFERING, SACRIFICE”; NSK “CASTER of metal objects”.

evidence.locator: SEM000276 nsk [pour] V, PUN001328 nsk [cast] V

cognates.note: Neo-Punic hnskt for the cast statues of Augustus, Germanicus and Drusus (KAI 122), and nskt for cast metal vessels (KAI 137).

evidence.note: “1. CAST METAL … 2. CAST METAL STATUE”.

cognates.note: The Phoenician form of מַסֵּכָה in the libation sense: Azatiwada brings a sacrifice “at all the mskt” (Karatepe, KAI 26 A II 17–III 2).

evidence.note: “[Heb. masseka] n.f. SEASONAL SACRIFICE, lit., LIBATION”.

cognates.note: Attested in Neo-Assyrian texts only, of tribal chiefs: the same word as נָסִיךְ, prince.

evidence.note: “sheikh; tribal leader”; Neo-Assyrian; also nasīkūtu “position of a sheikh”.

cognates.note: Set beside the Hebrew in the root lists, but its sense is throwing, not pouring; how it bears on נָסַךְ is not shown.

evidence.locator: SEM000276 nsk [pour] V, AKK008158 nasāku [throw (down)] V

cognates.gloss: worship; devote oneself to religious rites; (nasīka) a sacrificed victim; (manāsik) rites of the pilgrimage
cognates.note: A word of worship and sacrifice, not of pouring; it may be the same root narrowed to cultic acts, but nothing ties it to libation.

evidence.note: “He worshipped”; “He devoted himself to religious exercises”; نَسِيكَةٌ: see عَقِيقَةٌ (the victim sacrificed for a newborn).

doctrine.statement: Every burnt offering was to have its drink offering of wine, measured to the animal, poured out to Yahweh in the holy place as “a scent of pleasing” (Num 15:5–10; 28:7), at the daily offering and at every appointed time of Lev 23 (Lev 23:13, 18, 37). When David would not drink the water his men had brought at the risk of their lives, he poured it out to Yahweh, calling it their blood (2Sa 23:16–17), and the life is in the blood (Lev 17:11). Paul takes up the libation for himself: he is being poured out (σπένδομαι) on the sacrifice and service of the believers' faith, and at the end of his course is being poured out already (Php 2:17; 2Ti 4:6). From the verses: the drink offering was a life spent to the last drop for God, added to the offering it went with, and the apostle reads his own service and death that way.

Against the nations and kings who set themselves against Yahweh and his anointed, Yahweh says, “I have set (נָסַכְתִּי) my king on Zion, the mountain of my holiness”, gives him the nations for his inheritance and the ends of the earth for his possession, and says he will break them with a rod of iron (Psa 2:2, 6, 8–9). The apostles name the anointed: “your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed” (Act 4:25–27), and read “you are my son, today I have begotten you” of his being raised from the dead (Act 13:33; Psa 2:7). Revelation sees him ruling the nations with the rod of iron, and giving that rule to those who overcome (Rev 2:26–27; 19:15). From the verses: the king Yahweh sets on Zion is the risen Jesus, and his throne and rule are on the earth, over its nations.

In Pro 8 Wisdom is a woman who cries out in the streets and at the gates (8:1–3), who dwells with prudence (8:12), and who afterward builds her house and sets her table, set against the foolish woman (9:1–6, 13). She says Yahweh possessed her at the beginning of his way, and that she was set up, or formed, from everlasting, before the earth (8:22–23). Paul calls Christ “the wisdom of God”, who “became to us wisdom from God” (1Co 1:24, 30), and John says the word “became flesh” (Joh 1:14). From the verses: Pro 8 personifies God's own wisdom, with him before anything was made, and in Jesus that wisdom was made flesh; the chapter does not speak of a person existing before his birth.

The first מַסֵּכָה is the calf Aaron made of the people's gold, of which they said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt” (Exo 32:4); Stephen recalls it as an idol they sacrificed to (Act 7:41). The law at once forbids “gods of cast metal” (Exo 34:17; Lev 19:4) and curses the man who makes one (Deu 27:15). The prophets answer that it is the work of a craftsman who casts it and a smith who overlays it (Isa 40:19), that it is falsehood with no breath in it (Jer 10:14), and a teacher of lies, mute (Hab 2:18–19). From the verses: a god that has to be poured into a mould is no god, and to worship it is to worship the work of one's hands.

On his mountain Yahweh will swallow up “the covering that covers all the peoples, and the מַסֵּכָה woven over all the nations”; in the next breath “he will swallow up death for ever, and the Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from all faces” (Isa 25:7–8). Paul quotes those words of the dead raised incorruptible at Christ's coming: “Death is swallowed up in victory” (1Co 15:52–54). From the verses: the web spread over every nation is death, and it is taken away when the dead are raised.

note: BDB keys: the same tokens are filed under two keys three times (n.du.aa/n.dw.aa the verb, n.du.ac/n.dw.ab נָסִיךְ, n.du.ad/n.dv.ab מַסֵּכָה); this entry names one of each pair (n.du.aa, n.du.ac, n.du.ad) and gives the other senses (install, prince, covering) as senses of the same words. n.dv.aa (Isa 25:7, the passive “woven”) has its own token and is named on the verb. m.cr.ae and m.cr.af are BDB cross-references with no tokens. The weaving words (מַסֵּכָה in Isa 25:7 and 28:20, נְסוּכָה, מַסֶּכֶת) have no cognate under נסך; Hebrew סכך “cover, weave” (Psa 139:13) and Arabic nasaja “weave” (Lane p. 2787, with j, not a regular match for כ) are leads not followed. Syriac ܢܣܟ (libation; cast) not checked: the root is not in SEDRA, and Payne Smith was not consulted by page. Isa 30:1 מַסֵּכָה is filed as libation, after Phoenician mskt; “weave a web” is the other reading.
